claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To get started, I need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let me begin with the basics:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now, to assess your eligibility, I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. But no, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you currently, I need to understand your relationship to his upkeep:

**Are you making any financial contributions towards looking after Alex, such as payments for his food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out a bit with some money for him - I send money for clothes and things like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To properly assess your eligibility, I need to know more details about these contributions:

**Roughly how much do you contribute per week or per month towards Alex's upkeep (for clothes, food, and other expenses)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I send about £10 a week to help with his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. I need to understand the current Child Benefit payment amount to properly assess your situation. However, I also need to clarify one more important thing:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has a claim been made for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I have a clearer picture of your situation.

Based on what you've told me, I need to let you know that your current contributions of £10 per week may not be sufficient for you to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex under the rules.

Here's why: According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can normally get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after the child goes to live with them. After that, you can continue to receive it only if you contribute **at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment itself** towards the child's upkeep.

Before I make my final assessment, I need one more piece of information:

**How long has Alex been living away from you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living away for a couple of months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. Based on all the information you've provided, let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary of my decision:**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Why?**
- While you do live in the UK and are making contributions towards Alex's upkeep, the amount you're contributing (£10 per week) is below what's required to maintain eligibility
- When a child lives with someone else, you can normally receive Child Benefit for 8 weeks. Since Alex has been living away for a couple of months, you're now beyond that initial 8-week period
- To continue receiving Child Benefit after those 8 weeks, your contributions must equal or exceed the current Child Benefit payment rate (which is £21.15 per week for a child)
- Your contributions of £10 per week fall short of this requirement

**What you could do:**
If you were to increase your contributions to at least £21.15 per week or more, you may become eligible again. You would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss this and explain your increased contributions.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?
